title: Add a dropdown selector to `st.chat_input` similar to LLM chat interfaces
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary Add a dropdown selector to `st.chat_input`, similar to the pattern used in ChatGPT and other LLM chat interfaces. This could either: - extend the current `accept_file=True` behavior, or - be introduced as a separate selector component attached to `st.chat_input` Right now, this kind of UI is not really possible to implement cleanly without something like `st.bottom`. ### Why? For data analysis workflows, it is often important to specify exactly which dataset, table, or context the model should use. A selector attached to `st.chat_input` would make that context explicit before submission, which helps: - reduce ambiguity about which data the model should query - avoid hallucinated joins or incorrect assumptions across tables - support more targeted system prompts - make it easier to drive different output modes, such as plain text, charts, or HTML reports. **Example use case** A user might choose one of the following before sending a message: - a specific table - a semantic layer or query target - an output mode such as text, chart, or report That gives the app a structured way to route the prompt and configure the model behavior before the message is processed. ### How? _No response_ ### Additional Context _No response_
